1883.us: The Brooklyn Bridge opened in May, then the world’s longest suspension bridge. That autumn railroads adopted standard time zones, and the Supreme Court struck down the Civil Rights Act of 1875.
1883.latam: Chile and Peru signed the Treaty of Ancón in October, ending the war between them and costing Peru nitrate-rich Tarapacá. In Brazil, activists formed the Abolitionist Confederation to end slavery.
1883.europe: Germany passed Bismarck’s Health Insurance Law, the first national sickness insurance scheme. Karl Marx died in London in March, and Nietzsche published the first part of “Thus Spoke Zarathustra.”
1883.russia: Alexander III was crowned in Moscow in May, two years after his father’s assassination, and pressed a conservative crackdown. In Geneva, Georgi Plekhanov founded the first Russian Marxist group.
1883.mideast: Egypt was under British occupation, and Evelyn Baring arrived as consul-general. In Sudan, the Mahdi’s forces wiped out an Egyptian army under Hicks Pasha at Shaykan in November.
1883.africa: Paul Kruger became president of the Transvaal. On the coast of today’s Namibia, German merchant Adolf Lüderitz bought land at Angra Pequena, the seed of a German colony.
1883.india: The Ilbert Bill, letting Indian judges try Europeans in some cases, sparked fierce protest from British residents against Viceroy Lord Ripon. Nationalists held an Indian National Conference in Calcutta.
1883.china: France made Vietnam a protectorate in August and fought China-backed Black Flag forces in Tonkin, edging toward war with the Qing. In Tokyo, the Rokumeikan opened for Western-style balls.

1884.us: Grover Cleveland won the presidency in November, the first Democrat elected since before the Civil War. In December workers set the capstone on the Washington Monument.
1884.latam: Brazil’s province of Ceará abolished slavery in March, followed by Amazonas. Bolivia signed a truce leaving its coast to Chile, and Porfirio Díaz returned to Mexico’s presidency in December.
1884.europe: Britain’s Third Reform Act gave the vote to most rural male householders, and the socialist Fabian Society was founded in London. In November, Bismarck opened the Berlin Conference on Africa.
1884.russia: Russia annexed the Central Asian oasis of Merv, alarming Britain about India’s frontier. A new university statute ended university self-government as Alexander III tightened control.
1884.mideast: Britain sent General Charles Gordon to Khartoum to evacuate Egyptian garrisons from Sudan. By spring the Mahdi’s forces had him under siege.
1884.africa: Germany declared protectorates over South West Africa, Togoland and Cameroon. In November the Berlin Conference opened, speeding the European race for African land.
1884.india: Lord Dufferin replaced Lord Ripon as viceroy in December. In Pune, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and fellow nationalists founded the Deccan Education Society to run Indian-led schools.
1884.china: France and China fought openly: in August a French fleet destroyed China’s Fujian fleet at Fuzhou in under an hour. In Korea, pro-Japanese reformers’ Gapsin Coup collapsed after three days.

1890.us: Idaho and Wyoming became states, Wyoming the first with women’s suffrage. On 29 December US troops killed about 250 to 300 Lakota at Wounded Knee.
1890.latam: Argentina’s Revolution of the Park in July forced President Juárez Celman out, and its debts nearly sank London’s Barings bank. Brazil’s new republic was gripped by a speculative bubble, the Encilhamento.
1890.europe: Kaiser Wilhelm II forced Bismarck to resign in March. Britain swapped the North Sea island of Heligoland to Germany for Zanzibar, and Vincent van Gogh died in France.
1890.russia: Anton Chekhov crossed Siberia to study the penal colony on Sakhalin island. Heir Nicholas set off on a grand tour toward Asia, and a new law curbed the elected zemstvo councils.
1890.mideast: Persia’s Naser al-Din Shah granted a British company a monopoly over the country’s tobacco, a deal that would spark mass protest. Sultan Abdul Hamid II ruled the Ottoman Empire from Istanbul.
1890.africa: Cecil Rhodes became prime minister of the Cape Colony, and his Pioneer Column marched into Mashonaland, founding Fort Salisbury, today’s Harare. Zanzibar became a British protectorate.
1890.india: Britain and China signed a convention in Calcutta recognizing Sikkim as a British protectorate. A trial over the death of child bride Phulmoni fueled debate on the age of consent.
1890.china: Japan’s Meiji Constitution took effect, and the first Imperial Diet met in November after Japan’s first general election. In China, Zhang Zhidong began building the Hanyang Iron Works.

1898.us: After the Maine blew up, the US fought Spain from April to August and annexed Hawaii in July. In November a white mob overthrew the elected government of Wilmington, North Carolina.
1898.latam: US forces landed in Cuba and Puerto Rico, ending four centuries of Spanish rule there. In December’s Treaty of Paris, Spain gave up Cuba and ceded Puerto Rico to the US.
1898.europe: Émile Zola’s “J’accuse…!” blew open the Dreyfus Affair in France. Germany passed its first Navy Law, Bismarck died in July, and an anarchist assassinated Austria’s Empress Elisabeth in Geneva.
1898.russia: Marxists met in Minsk to found the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party. Russia leased Port Arthur from China, and the new Moscow Art Theatre staged Chekhov’s “The Seagull.”
1898.mideast: Kaiser Wilhelm II toured the Ottoman Empire, riding into Jerusalem and visiting Saladin’s tomb in Damascus. On the Nile, an Anglo-Egyptian army crushed the Mahdist state at Omdurman.
1898.africa: At Fashoda in Sudan, British and French forces faced off over the upper Nile, nearly causing war. In Sierra Leone, Bai Bureh led the Hut Tax War against British rule.
1898.india: Bubonic plague, raging since 1896, spread from Bombay to Calcutta, and harsh British controls provoked anger. In December, Swami Vivekananda consecrated Belur Math near Calcutta.
1898.china: The Guangxu Emperor’s Hundred Days’ Reform ended in September when Empress Dowager Cixi took control. Germany, Russia and Britain seized leases, including Hong Kong’s New Territories for 99 years.

1906.us: An earthquake and fires destroyed much of San Francisco in April. After Upton Sinclair’s “The Jungle,” Congress passed the Pure Food and Drug Act and the Meat Inspection Act.
1906.latam: The US occupied Cuba again in September after a revolt, and an earthquake devastated Valparaíso, Chile. In Mexico, a strike at the Cananea copper mine was crushed.
1906.europe: Liberals won a British landslide, and 29 Labour MPs entered Parliament. France cleared Alfred Dreyfus, and the Algeciras Conference settled a Franco-German crisis over Morocco.
1906.russia: Russia’s first elected parliament, the State Duma, opened in May and was dissolved after ten weeks. New prime minister Pyotr Stolypin launched land reforms and field courts against revolutionaries.
1906.mideast: Protests forced Persia’s shah to grant a constitution, and the first Majlis met in October. In Egypt, British courts hanged four villagers after the Denshawai incident, stirring nationalist anger.
1906.africa: Zulu chief Bambatha led a revolt against a poll tax in Natal, crushed with heavy loss of life. In German East Africa, the Maji Maji uprising was being brutally suppressed.
1906.india: The All-India Muslim League was founded in Dhaka in December. Bengalis boycotted British goods over the partition of Bengal, and Dadabhai Naoroji called for swaraj, self-rule.
1906.china: The Qing court announced it would prepare for a constitution, a year after abolishing the old civil service exams. Japan founded the South Manchuria Railway Company.

1907.us: A banking panic in October was calmed when J.P. Morgan organized a rescue. Oklahoma became a state, and the Great White Fleet set off around the world in December.
1907.latam: In Chile, soldiers massacred striking nitrate miners and their families at a school in Iquique in December. Central American states met in Washington and created a Central American Court of Justice.
1907.europe: Britain and Russia settled their rivalry in the Anglo-Russian Convention, forming the Triple Entente with France. Delegates met at the Second Hague Peace Conference, and Picasso painted “Les Demoiselles d’Avignon.”
1907.russia: In June, Stolypin dissolved the Second Duma and rewrote election rules to favor landowners. Russia and Britain settled their Asian rivalry in the Anglo-Russian Convention.
1907.mideast: The Anglo-Russian Convention split Persia into Russian and British spheres without asking Persians. In Egypt, Lord Cromer retired, and Mustafa Kamil founded the Nationalist Party.
1907.africa: In the Transvaal, Mohandas Gandhi led Indians in resisting the “Black Act” requiring them to register. In German East Africa, the Maji Maji rebellion ended after famine killed tens of thousands.
1907.india: The Indian National Congress split between moderates and radicals at its Surat session. Punjab leader Lala Lajpat Rai was deported to Mandalay, and Tata Iron and Steel was founded.
1907.china: Revolutionary Qiu Jin was executed by the Qing in July. Japan forced Korea’s Emperor Gojong to abdicate and disbanded the Korean army.

1908.us: William Howard Taft won the presidential election, and the Bureau of Investigation, forerunner of the FBI, was founded. Orville Wright demonstrated his airplane to the Army at Fort Myer.
1908.latam: Juan Vicente Gómez seized power in Venezuela in December, starting a 27-year rule. In Mexico, Porfirio Díaz told a US journalist the country was ready for democracy.
1908.europe: Austria-Hungary annexed Bosnia and Herzegovina, enraging Serbia, and Bulgaria declared full independence. London hosted the Olympic Games, and Wilbur Wright amazed crowds flying in France.
1908.russia: On 30 June a huge explosion, likely an incoming meteor or comet, flattened about 2,000 square km of forest near Tunguska, Siberia. Russia was humiliated in the Bosnian crisis.
1908.mideast: The Young Turk Revolution forced Sultan Abdul Hamid II to restore the constitution. In Persia, British prospectors struck oil at Masjed Soleyman, and the Hejaz Railway reached Medina.
1908.africa: Belgium annexed the Congo Free State from King Leopold II after reports of mass atrocities. Delegates from four British colonies met to plan a Union of South Africa.
1908.india: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was jailed for six years in Mandalay for sedition. Eighteen-year-old Khudiram Bose was hanged after a bomb attack in Muzaffarpur.
1908.china: The Guangxu Emperor and Empress Dowager Cixi died a day apart in November. Puyi, aged two, became the last Qing emperor.

1912.us: Woodrow Wilson won a four-way presidential race against Taft, Theodore Roosevelt and Eugene Debs. New Mexico and Arizona became states, and textile workers struck in Lawrence, Massachusetts.
1912.latam: US Marines landed in Nicaragua to prop up its government. Argentina’s Sáenz Peña Law brought secret, compulsory male voting, and Mexico’s President Madero fought off rebellions.
1912.europe: Stockholm hosted the Summer Olympics. In October, Serbia, Bulgaria, Greece and Montenegro attacked the Ottoman Empire in the First Balkan War, seizing most of its European lands.
1912.russia: Troops fired on striking workers at the Lena goldfields in Siberia, killing or wounding hundreds and sparking strikes nationwide. The Bolsheviks launched their newspaper Pravda in St. Petersburg.
1912.mideast: Italy took Libya from the Ottoman Empire in the Treaty of Ouchy in October, as Balkan armies advanced on Istanbul. France made Morocco a protectorate under the Treaty of Fez.
1912.africa: In January, Black leaders meeting in Bloemfontein founded the South African Native National Congress, later the ANC. Frederick Lugard returned to Nigeria to merge its northern and southern protectorates.
1912.india: Delhi became the new capital of British India in place of Calcutta. In December a bomb wounded Viceroy Lord Hardinge as he rode an elephant into Delhi.
1912.china: The last Qing emperor, Puyi, abdicated in February, ending over 2,000 years of imperial rule, and Yuan Shikai became president. In Japan, Emperor Meiji died, opening the Taishō era.

1916.us: Pancho Villa raided Columbus, New Mexico, and US troops chased him into Mexico. Wilson won reelection on “He kept us out of war,” and Montana elected Jeannette Rankin, the first congresswoman.
1916.latam: US Marines occupied the Dominican Republic, staying until 1924. Argentina held its first presidential election by secret ballot and chose Hipólito Yrigoyen of the Radical Civic Union.
1916.europe: Germany and France bled at Verdun for ten months, and the British and German fleets clashed off Jutland. In Dublin, Irish republicans launched the Easter Rising.
1916.russia: General Brusilov’s summer offensive smashed Austro-Hungarian lines but cost huge losses. In December, nobles murdered Rasputin, the mystic who influenced the royal family.
1916.mideast: Sharif Hussein of Mecca launched the Arab Revolt against Ottoman rule in June. In April, a besieged British-Indian army surrendered to the Ottomans at Kut in Mesopotamia.
1916.africa: Allied troops under Jan Smuts pushed into German East Africa against Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck’s forces. In Ethiopia, Lij Iyasu was deposed, and Zewditu became empress with Ras Tafari as regent.
1916.india: Congress and the Muslim League agreed the Lucknow Pact, a joint demand for self-government. Tilak and Annie Besant founded Home Rule Leagues, while Indian troops fought in Mesopotamia.
1916.china: Yuan Shikai tried to make himself emperor, gave up after provinces revolted, and died in June. China slid into the warlord era.

1918.us: Wilson set out his Fourteen Points for peace in January. Over a million US troops fought in the Meuse-Argonne Offensive, and Congress passed the Sedition Act, curbing criticism of the war.
1918.latam: Students in Córdoba, Argentina, launched a university reform movement that spread across Latin America. Brazil, the only South American country at war, sent a naval squadron and doctors to Europe.
1918.europe: Germany’s spring offensive failed, and the Armistice ended the fighting on 11 November. The Kaiser abdicated, Austria-Hungary broke apart, and many British women over 30 gained the vote.
1918.russia: The Bolsheviks signed the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk with Germany in March, giving up vast lands, and moved the capital to Moscow. Civil war spread, and the royal family was shot in July.
1918.mideast: British and Arab forces took Damascus in October, and the Ottoman Empire signed the Armistice of Mudros on 30 October, ending its war. Allied ships soon anchored off Istanbul.
1918.africa: The Spanish flu spread along ports and railways, killing an estimated 300,000 in South Africa alone. Lettow-Vorbeck’s German force surrendered in Northern Rhodesia two weeks after the Armistice.
1918.india: Influenza killed an estimated 12 million or more Indians, the highest toll anywhere. Gandhi led protests in Kheda and Ahmedabad, and the Montagu-Chelmsford Report proposed limited self-rule.
1918.china: In Japan, soaring rice prices sparked riots, and Hara Takashi became the first commoner prime minister. Japan sent troops into Siberia, and in China Lu Xun published “A Madman’s Diary.”

1923.us: President Warren Harding died in August, and Calvin Coolidge was sworn in by his father by lamplight in Vermont. Time magazine launched, and the Hollywoodland sign went up.
1923.latam: Pancho Villa was assassinated in July. Mexico and the US signed the Bucareli Agreements, and Washington recognized Álvaro Obregón’s government.
1923.europe: General Primo de Rivera seized power in Spain in September. In Munich, Adolf Hitler’s Beer Hall Putsch failed in November, and the Irish Civil War ended in May.
1923.russia: Lenin was disabled by a stroke in March, and a power struggle grew among Stalin, Trotsky and others. The new Soviet Union approved its first constitution.
1923.mideast: The Treaty of Lausanne set Turkey’s borders, and on 29 October Mustafa Kemal proclaimed the Republic of Turkey with Ankara as capital. Egypt adopted a constitution under King Fuad.
1923.africa: Ethiopia joined the League of Nations, and Southern Rhodesia’s white settlers gained self-government. In Kenya, a British white paper declared African interests paramount.
1923.india: C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru launched the Swaraj Party to contest elections and fight British rule from inside the councils, while Gandhi sat in prison.
1923.china: The Great Kantō earthquake on 1 September destroyed much of Tokyo and Yokohama, killing over 100,000. In China, Sun Yat-sen allied with the Soviet Union to rebuild his Nationalist party.
